thread.title: Foxconn unit wins CSRC approval for Shanghai IPO: sources

author: Reuters Editorial
title: Foxconn unit wins CSRC approval for Shanghai IPO: sources
text:
SHANGHAI (Reuters) - Taiwan’s Foxconn ( 2317.TW ), the world’s largest contract electronics manufacturer, has won approval for a mainland listing of an internet and industrial-focused subsidiary, two sources said on Thursday.
FILE PHOTO: Logos of Foxconn and Ennoconn are seen during the annual Computex computer exhibition in Taipei, Taiwan June 1, 2016. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu/File Photo Foxconn, formally known as Hon Hai Precision Industry Co, has been aiming to list the unit, Foxconn Industrial Internet Co Ltd (FII), on the Shanghai Stock Exchange to help fund projects in smart manufacturing, cloud computing and 5G solutions.
The firm said previously that around 10 percent of the unit’s shares would be converted to floating stock, with parent Foxconn holding onto around 85 percent of the shares. Foxconn shareholders approved the plan in January.
Last month, the company said it planned to use proceeds from the listing to fund eight projects totaling 27.3 billion yuan ($4.31 billion). The subsidiary unit makes electronic devices, cloud service equipment and industrial robots.
Foxconn Industrial Internet made a net profit of 16.2 billion yuan in 2017 and lists clients such as Amazon.com Inc ( AMZN.O ), Apple Inc ( AAPL.O ) Cisco Systems ( CSCO.O ), Dell [DI.UL], Huawei [HWT.UL] and Lenovo ( 0992.HK ).
Reuters could not immediately reach Foxconn or the subsidiary for comment on Thursday.
Reporting by Xiaochong Zhang and Adam JourdanAdditional reporting by SHANGHAI newsroom; Editing by Shri Navaratnam
